# Recreation Prompt

Recreate `Throne of Petty Houses` as a portrait-first browser-native canvas strategy game. Preserve the source mechanic truth: a real-time graph conquest map where the player selects a starting region, starts the match, drags from owned adjacent regions to send half of the current count, troops travel along edges, allied arrivals reinforce, enemy arrivals subtract and can capture, capital capture annexes whole factions, AI sends its own packets, a timed defensive ability deters enemy targeting, speed/pause/restart remain available, all enemies defeated wins, and no player regions/troops loses.

The public identity should be a satirical dynasty strategy drama inspired by medieval court power games: rival petty houses, absurd bloodline claims, dragon intimidation, icy apocalypse omens, betrayal, crowns, parchment war table, heraldic shields, gold/blood/ice palette, regal but readable typography, mobile-safe touch targets, and concise HUD copy that always tells the real action.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source Game Truth
- genre: real-time graph/territorial conquest strategy on a canvas map.
- objective: select a starting region, dispatch half of an owned region's forces to adjacent regions, capture enemy capitals, annex factions, and end with every enemy region removed.
- input model: mobile-safe pointer taps for starting-house selection; pointer drag from owned region to adjacent target for dispatch; HUD buttons for defensive cooldown, speed, pause, resume, music, track, restart, and quit.
- core loop: regions produce counts over time, player and AI send troop packets, arriving packets reinforce allies or subtract enemy counts, captured capitals flip the loser faction, victory/loss checks run each frame.
- fail/friction state: no player-owned regions and no player troops causes defeat; invalid drag or disabled defensive ability gives blocked feedback; devastated regions have reduced capacity.

## Protected Mechanics
- Preserve graph adjacency, polygon hit detection, 50% dispatch amount, troop travel by distance/base speed, production cadence, AI cadence, capital annex semantics, cooldown/duration semantics, speed cycle, pause/restart flow, and win/loss rules.

## Safe Presentation Surfaces
Title, copy, HUD vocabulary, fonts, colors, faction names, region labels, canvas rendering style, background motifs, feedback captions, toast wording, button styling, and audio/track labels are safe to transform because they do not alter gameplay rules.
